title: Shonen Jump’s Newest and Hottest Leading Manga Is Fixing One of Shonen’s Biggest Flaws
content:
Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump has produced some of the most prominent manga series for decades. However, even among its waves of amazing shonen manga, one element has consistently been lacking, and this new manga series is fixing it perfectly. The term shonen itself refers to young boys, which is why the genre has often been criticized for its lack of well-written female characters. While many series do include female characters, they are often relegated to slapstick comedy and stereotypical roles, frequently portrayed as fawning over male characters characterized as studs. Even great series like Naruto have been criticized for their poor female character writing.

However, as times have changed, so has shonen manga, including its approach to female characters. The Naruto sequel itself is a recent example , as Sarada Uchiha has proven her worth, while her dynamic with Sumire, involving a romantic element, demonstrates that female characters can shine even in stories with romantic plots. However, what Ichi the Witch , one of the hottest and newest leading shonen series, has accomplished is arguably something few shonen series have done before. By placing female characters at the forefront and featuring only a few male characters, Ichi the Witch has subverted a common shonen trope and delivered the character development that female characters in the genre have always deserved.

Shonen Jump’s Hottest New Series Has the Perfect Cheat Code for Fixing Female Characters in Shonen

Ichi the Witch is set in a world where only biological females can wield magic and become witches. This premise already establishes that the series will feature many female characters at the forefront, despite having a male lead who becomes a witch under special circumstances. The series never forgets its foundation, constantly reminding readers that its female characters are its soul. This is best demonstrated in the latest chapter, Ichi the Witch Chapter 101, titled “To the Beyond.” It features Kumugi Harvest, a prominent member of Ichi’s team, as she finally unveils her true power. Kumugi was always portrayed as a nerd with limited magical prowess and seemingly weak characteristics.

However, the latest chapter confirms that she always had the potential to become stronger, more so than many female characters depicted in the genre. Kumugi had simply forgotten her abilities because of the trauma caused by her overwhelming power. But after remembering her potential and accepting her scars, she immediately emerges as a strong character. Her growth reflects the kind of great character writing that most shonen series have traditionally reserved for their male leads. This highlights how shonen manga has often held female characters back by focusing on male protagonists and relegating women to supporting roles and slapstick comedy.

However, times have changed, and more series have begun embracing deeper characterization for female characters. Ichi the Witch is the perfect example of this revolutionary change. While some critics might believe this approach won’t work for shonen manga, the series’ sales prove that it is performing well and establishing itself as a leading manga of the modern era. With its perfect blend of shonen fantasy and grounded character development, Ichi the Witch has emerged as a leading modern shonen series , and its popularity is only expected to grow.

title: Boruto: Two Blue Vortex Chapter 38 Hints at Naruto’s Shocking Return
content:
Boruto: Two Blue Vortex is returning with its monthly release, and as always, a week before the chapter’s release, it has revealed a sneak peek. Chapter 38 will be featured in the upcoming V-Jump issue, releasing on Tuesday, October 20, in Western regions. Currently, the series is at a crucial point, with Sarada abducted and Boruto in the process of rescuing her. With Kashin Koji refusing to aid the protagonist and the danger of Boruto turning into Momoshiki looming, the series has a lot going on. This is why the latest chapter’s sneak peek might come as a surprise, as it strongly hints at Naruto’s return.

It is known that Kawaki trapped Naruto and Hinata in a space that no one can access except him. Kawaki did this to protect Naruto, but it was evident that Naruto’s return was inevitable at some point . Now, it seems the stage for his return has been set, as the sneak peek for Chapter 38 shows Kawaki in this special place. While the series has shown Kawaki visiting this place before, the most notable detail in this instance is that he is apologizing to them, suggesting that he might be ready to redeem himself and free Naruto. Additionally, there is one more element that hints at why Naruto’s return might be necessary.

Boruto: Two Blue Vortex Chapter 38 Hints That Kawaki Is Preparing to Bring Back Naruto

The specific reason why Naruto’s return might be necessary is that Shikamaru, the current Hokage of Konoha, is facing significant backlash from Kobu , the representative of the Fire Nation Daimyo, over the way he is doing his job. Shikamaru is suspected of being a spy or an ally of Boruto, who is blamed for Naruto’s death. At some point, the tide has to turn in the hero’s favor, and Naruto’s return could be what fixes the situation. It would not only resolve Shikamaru’s current predicament but also clear Boruto of the murder accusations, allowing him to reclaim his identity.

Meanwhile, another factor supporting Naruto’s return is how much Boruto might need his father in the future. Kashin Koji’s prescience has revealed the possibility of Boruto being overtaken by Momoshiki, and Naruto could be the trigger that brings Boruto back to his original self. This could also give fans an emotional reunion between father and son. Overall, Naruto’s return is long overdue, as he has always been a major part of the franchise, and leaving him uninvolved in the series’ final events would be an oversight. Perhaps this is also why the surprising return of Naruto in a manga by the original author could be significant.

It was recently announced that a new manga series by Masashi Kishimoto would tell a story set between the events of Naruto Shippuden and Naruto becoming Hokage . There is considerable merit in considering that this manga could properly bridge the gap between the Naruto and Boruto series. It could also establish Naruto and Sasuke as central figures in Boruto ‘s endgame. This could mean that Boruto is setting the stage not only for Naruto ‘s return but also for Sasuke’s return very soon, and upcoming chapters of Boruto: Two Blue Vortex could confirm this, especially given that Hidari, the Divine Tree imitation of Sasuke, could soon be defeated by Sarada.

title: 50 Years Ago, This Magical Girl Manga Sparked An Entire Genre
content:
Go Nagai, a legendary manga artist and writer best known for his magnum opus Devilman is, unsurprisingly, one of the most influential figures in manga, being a trendsetter whose unconventional creativity and art influenced series like Berserk , Neon Genesis Evangelion , as well western properties like Transformers and Pacific Rim , it shouldn’t be surprising that Go Nagai’s work would have the power to influence an entire genre. In 1973, he did just that with the release of Cutie Honey , an offbeat magical girl manga that, while not the first of its kind, popularized and laid the foundation for the “magical girl warrior” trope, building on early magical girl concepts like Osamu Tezuka’s 1953 series Princess Knight and The Secret of Akko-chan , created by Fujio Akatsuka in 1962.

Cutie Honey built on the early framework for what the magical girl could be and turned the dial up to eleven, making its protagonist into a defiant action-focused hero with flashy transformations that would later inspire successors like Sailor Moon . Plus, Cutie Honey is widely recognized for being one of the first shonen manga to feature a solo female protagonist as opposed to having a male lead. While the series is still considered relatively niche among western anime fans despite being released fifty years ago, Cutie Honey has remained one of the most influential pieces of magical girl fiction and shonen manga in Japan.

Cutie Honey Is A Bombastic, Self-Aware Masterpiece

Like with all of Go Nagai’s work, Cutie Honey is hilariously over-the-top and knows exactly what it is. The original manga is perfectly campy, and with every new spin on the character or adaptation of Honey’s origins and adventures, audiences can expect the humor and action to blend seamlessly in creating something that is infectiously fun to watch. Go Nagai’s original Cutie Honey manga follows Honey Kisaragi, an average Catholic schoolgirl whose father is suddenly murdered by the elusive organization known as Panther Claw.

She soon learns that she’s actually a hyper-advanced android with a mechanism inside her that allows her to transform into a super-powered, red-haired heroine called Cutie Honey. Mischievous and full of charm, Cutie Honey embarks on a quest for revenge to discover who killed her father, and why the organization wanted her dead in the first place.

Cutie Honey has had numerous iterations following the success of Go Nagai’s work . Interestingly, while the original manga was considered a shonen manga, it was originally intended to be a shojo — something that was made possible with the release of Cutie Honey Flash , a 1997 animation project from Toei Animation and Go Nagai that reimagined Nagai’s original character design in a style skin to that of Sailor Moon . Cutie Honey received multiple spin-offs, sequels, live-action and anime projects, all of which having some input of Go Nagai in the handling of Honey, even if the series has unique artists or writing teams involved, even receiving multiple stage play projects.

How Go Nagai’s Original Work Shaped The Future Of Magical Girl Anime

While Cutie Honey may seem unconventional compared to its modern contemporaries, that doesn’t mean the series didn’t have a massive impact at the peak of its popularity. As previously mentioned, the concept of the “magical girl warrior” seen in franchises like Sailor Moon and Cardcaptor Sakura were heavily influences by Cutie Honey , with Sailor V — Sailor Venus’s original alter ego in Sailor Moon , even using the exact same callout as Honey to pay homage to Go Nagai’s original series.

DokiDoki! Precure contains similar references, with one of its characters, Mamo, turns into a hero named “Cutie Madame” in one of the anime’s episodes. Funnily enough, Cutie Honey took inspiration from the same series inspired by it, with the aforementioned Cutie Honey Flash borrowing production staff from Toei Animation’s adaptation of Sailor Moon to give the anime a more contemporary shojo feel.

Needless to say, Cutie Honey is a massively influential franchise that, despite being relatively underground among western anime fans has created a ripple effect that can still be felt throughout the anime and manga industries. The series itself was inspired by timeless tokusatsu icons , building on that concept with outside influences from manga focusing on predominantly female heroes to create something inventive and fun. In that, Cutie Honey has succeeded in becoming timeless as well, with new projects featuring the super-powered android heroine still being produced as recently as 2018.

title: Major Shonen Jump Series Reveals It’s Starting Its Final Battle At Last
content:
Witch Watch is finally entering its final battle in the next chapter, which means that the ending is closer than you think. Kenta Shinohara’s hit Weekly Shonen Jump series follows a refreshing story set in a modern world where mythological and fantasy creatures have evolved and learned to live among humans. The manga began serialization in February 2021, and more than five years later, the story is finally closer to its finale. The information comes from @WSJ_manga on X, a reliable source of information for Shonen Jump fans. Although the release date hasn’t been confirmed, the manga entering the final battle means that it will take only a few months for the story to reach its conclusion.

While the series was already popular enough, it reached new heights of popularity after its anime debut in April 2025. The TV anime managed to get a huge fan following thanks to the heartwarming story, comedic elements, and, of course, gorgeous visuals. The anime was also confirmed to have a second season a while ago, although further details haven’t been announced yet. While fans await the anime’s return, the manga entered Part 3 and is now heading towards its anticipated finale. Last year, the manga confirmed that the ending has been delayed as the story gets more intense in its final stage. Following the delay, the story is all set to solve the unanswered questions and conclude the journey of Nico Wakatsuki and her friends.

Does Witch Watch Season 2 Have a Release Date?

Although the second season was announced a year ago, fans are still awaiting updates on the anime’s return. The first season concluded its two cours last year, leaving a majority of the questions unanswered. As the story keeps getting more intense with plot twists and mysteries, the animation studio stays silent on the second season. However, fans will get a major update on the series during this year’s Jump Festa .

It’s the largest annual convention held by Shueisha, as it focuses on new announcements for anime, manga, and games, interactive exhibits, and unique merchandise that is often available only at the convention. As confirmed on Jump Festa’s official website , Witch Watch will be holding a panel during the Jump Studio stage. While there hasn’t been any news on what the announcement will be, we can expect something related to the anime sequel and the manga finale.

What to Expect From Witch Watch Season 2

While the manga is heading towards its ending, the anime has a huge chunk of story left to adapt. The manga is split across three parts, and the first season only adapts around half of Part 1. The story finally takes shape in the second cour of the anime when Nico gets new familiars who begin living under the same roof as her and Morihito. Not to mention that the truth about the prophecy might also come to light sooner than expected. The episode count of the sequel season hasn’t been revealed yet, which is why it’s impossible to determine how many chapters will be adapted. However, there’s a good chance that the second season will wrap up the first part of the manga, which will finally reveal the threat looming over Nico’s head. Additionally, fans will also be introduced to new characters, both allies and enemies alike.

title: I Think Dragon Ball Should Follow One Piece’s Lead With a Live-Action Return
content:
Dragonball Evolution was released 17 and a half years ago , and it’s a flop on par with the Star Wars Holiday Special , but should that one release end the franchise’s future live-action prospects? No, Dragon Ball should absolutely return as a live-action product. In fact, the fan base should be in favor of the idea more than ever before with what One Piece accomplished in its first two seasons on Netflix.

Now, this idea does come with the obvious caveat of staying true to the cornerstones of the show’s foundation. Nevertheless, numerous IPs could give Dragon Ball a revival or road map. I’m excited at what it could look like in the hands of a director that understands the story. It could broaden the fanbase while still adding another installment that longtime fans can appreciate .

Live-Action Anime Just Needs Care

For those that don’t want to remember, Dragonball Evolution tanked and featured nothing close to the source material. Goku’s personality was more serious and not as lighthearted. The original work always merged a funny side tone with potential world-ending battles. The movie didn’t understand that unique blend that made the animated series so enthralling. As a lifelong One Piece fan and 20-plus year reader of the original manga , I was a massive skeptic that its live-action series would do the same.

After just watching what Paramount+ had done with Halo a year earlier, I was out. For more than two decades, the games never revealed what Master Chief’s face looked like, and the streaming service decided to show it in less than one episode of airtime. An immediate turn off for longtime fans. The fact that the team in charge of the Halo show specifically wanted to create an original story isn’t bad overall. It was the lack of care shown for how the game portrayed those characters.

The thought that someone might do the same to One Piece was definitely worrisome. Would the director try to create a whole new storyline or change a character’s identifiable characteristics? Would Gum-Gum Fruit attacks look incredibly awkward and out of place when it’s not in an animated form? And when the show dropped, it was exactly the opposite of what I was expecting. The characters were faithful to their roots.

Yes, the adaptation featured some changes, but they didn’t subtract from the story. For instance ( SPOILERS AHEAD ), One Piece introduced Vice Admiral Monkey D. Garp in the first season of the live action as Luffy’s grandfather. The same plot point isn’t revealed until years later in the anime. The detail wasn’t wrong, but the timeline was just adjusted in order to move the plot along .

Casting Is Key For Next Dragon Ball Live-Action Attempt

One of the most important pieces of One Piece ’s success is that those in charge cast the perfect actor for series protagonist Monkey D. Luffy. Iñaki Godoy dove headfirst into the role and made Luffy’s personality look real, which is no easy task considering he’s a man made of rubber. Just like Goku, Luffy’s over-the-top, cartoony goofiness can become a caricature easily or, even worse, one-dimensional. Godoy made the character’s move to TV appear seamless. He brought Luffy’s trademark impossible optimism, fiercely loyal friendship and unbeatable spirit to life.

On the contrary in Dragonball Evolution , Goku was not even remotely close to the kind-hearted, jovial, while simultaneously, powerful Saiyan fighter from the anime . In the movie, he has to deal with bullies, lacks plenty of the previously mentioned humor and is a little more cocky. It felt like they tried to combine his character with Vegeta at times. It proved that the director and script are always paramount when it comes to these decisions, and it didn’t connect with Dragonball Evolution .

It’s understandable that editing these works can be difficult, but that’s where the people involved should be reading the original works. Any anime is difficult to produce an exact carbon copy for the big screen or American TV. Between filler episodes, a bevy of one-off characters and mature subject matter, it’s impossible to completely retell the story exactly the same. However, a faithful retelling of Dragon Ball can still occur with a fresh take and some tweaks.

In addition to what One Piece put out, there are multiple other live-action anime that proved to be of quality too. The American comic book industry is saturated with one successful reboot after another too, so there’s a pattern already in place. When one movie or show falls flat on its face, another creative team finds a way to breathe new life into it. When Batman and Robin was panned, the franchise went dormant for nearly a decade until Christopher Nolan picked it up and turned it into the gritty, dark, vengeful tale that everyone grew up on.

There’s still hope that Dragon Ball can make its return with a new a live-action entity. It just needs to be done the right way with a creative team that approaches it with the fans in mind. Do you think Dragon Ball could work with a new live-action series like One Piece ? What do you think it would need to succeed? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

As a lifelong One Piece fan and 20-plus year reader of the original manga , I was a massive skeptic that its live-action series would do the same.

After just watching what Paramount+ had done with Halo a year earlier, I was out. For more than two decades, the games never revealed what Master Chief’s face looked like, and the streaming service decided to show it in less than one episode of airtime. An immediate turn off for longtime fans. The fact that the team in charge of the Halo show specifically wanted to create an original story isn’t bad overall. It was the lack of care shown for how the game portrayed those characters.

The thought that someone might do the same to One Piece was definitely worrisome. Would the director try to create a whole new storyline or change a character’s identifiable characteristics? Would Gum-Gum Fruit attacks look incredibly awkward and out of place when it’s not in an animated form? And when the show dropped, it was exactly the opposite of what I was expecting. The characters were faithful to their roots.

Yes, the adaptation featured some changes, but they didn’t subtract from the story. For instance ( SPOILERS AHEAD ), One Piece introduced Vice Admiral Monkey D. Garp in the first season of the live action as Luffy’s grandfather. The same plot point isn’t revealed until years later in the anime. The detail wasn’t wrong, but the timeline was just adjusted in order to move the plot along .
Casting Is Key For Next Dragon Ball Live-Action Attempt

One of the most important pieces of One Piece ’s success is that those in charge cast the perfect actor for series protagonist Monkey D. Luffy. Iñaki Godoy dove headfirst into the role and made Luffy’s personality look real, which is no easy task considering he’s a man made of rubber. Just like Goku, Luffy’s over-the-top, cartoony goofiness can become a caricature easily or, even worse, one-dimensional. Godoy made the character’s move to TV appear seamless. He brought Luffy’s trademark impossible optimism, fiercely loyal friendship and unbeatable spirit to life.

On the contrary in Dragonball Evolution , Goku was not even remotely close to the kind-hearted, jovial, while simultaneously, powerful Saiyan fighter from the anime . In the movie, he has to deal with bullies, lacks plenty of the previously mentioned humor and is a little more cocky. It felt like they tried to combine his character with Vegeta at times. It proved that the director and script are always paramount when it comes to these decisions, and it didn’t connect with Dragonball Evolution .

It’s understandable that editing these works can be difficult, but that’s where the people involved should be reading the original works. Any anime is difficult to produce an exact carbon copy for the big screen or American TV. Between filler episodes, a bevy of one-off characters and mature subject matter, it’s impossible to completely retell the story exactly the same. However, a faithful retelling of Dragon Ball can still occur with a fresh take and some tweaks.

In addition to what One Piece put out, there are multiple other live-action anime that proved to be of quality too. The American comic book industry is saturated with one successful reboot after another too, so there’s a pattern already in place. When one movie or show falls flat on its face, another creative team finds a way to breathe new life into it. When Batman and Robin was panned, the franchise went dormant for nearly a decade until Christopher Nolan picked it up and turned it into the gritty, dark, vengeful tale that everyone grew up on.

There’s still hope that Dragon Ball can make its return with a new a live-action entity. It just needs to be done the right way with a creative team that approaches it with the fans in mind. Do you think Dragon Ball could work with a new live-action series like One Piece ? What do you think it would need to succeed? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Cregger's Resident Evil Opens at #2 in Japan, 5th Girls und Panzer das Finale Film Opens at #5
content:
Eiga Chiikawa: Ningyo no Shima no Himitsu ( Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of Mermaid Island), the first anime film adaptation of Nagano 's Chiikawa manga, rose from #4 to #1 in its 12th weekend in Japan's box office. The film sold 375,000 tickets and earned 562,647,900 yen (about US$3.56 million) from Friday to Sunday.

The film has sold a total of 12.29 million tickets, and earned a cumulative total of 17,807,643,600 yen (about US$112 million). The film is currently the biggest film in Japan this year, and now ranks 12th in Japan's all-time box office ranking.

Eiga Chiikawa: Ningyo no Shima no Himitsu opened on July 24 and ranked at #1 for its opening weekend. The film earned 990 million yen (about US$6.05 million) on its opening day. The film sold 1,508,500 tickets and earned 2,240,333,500 yen (about US$13.70 million) in its first three days.

The film's 4DX screenings began on September 5. One-day-only cheering screenings for the film took place on September 11. Penlight screenings took place on September 23.

The film is based on the manga's arc posted on X (formerly Twitter ) from March to November 2023, nicknamed the "Siren Arc" or "Island Arc."

Nagano is credited for the original story and also wrote the film's script. Under Nagano 's supervision, Kei Oikawa ( Uma Musume Pretty Derby 3 seasons, Hinamatsuri , My Teen Romantic Comedy SNAFU TOO! , My Teen Romantic Comedy SNAFU Climax ) directed the film at Cygames Pictures . QTORY inc. managed the production, and TOHO is distributing the film.

The live-action film reboot of CAPCOM 's Resident Evil survival horror game franchise ranked at #2 in its opening weekend in Japan. The film sold 356,000 tickets and earned 626,567,150 yen (about US$3.97 million) in its first three days. The film sold 470,000 tickets to earn 813 million yen (about US$5.15 million) in its first four days (Monday, October 12 was a national holiday in Japan).

The film opened in Japan on October 9.

The film opened in the United States on September 18. The film ranked at #1 and earned an estimated US$60 million in its opening weekend in the U.S.

The film stars Austin Abrams ( Weapons , Euphoria , Wolfs ) as Bryan. The cast also includes Zach Cherry , Kali Reis , and Paul Walter Hauser ( Richard Jewell , Black Bird , The Fantastic Four: First Steps ).

Zach Cregger ( Barbarian , Weapons ) directed the new film.

The fifth film in the six-part Girls und Panzer das Finale film series ranked at #5 in its opening weekend. The film earned 267,301,400 yen (about US$1.69 million) in its first three days.

The film opened in Japan on October 9. The film is screening in Dolby Cinema, Dolby Atmos, 4DX, and MX4D, in addition to normal screenings. This marks the first time the film series is playing in Dolby Cinema.

The fifth film is set after Ōarai Girls High School's win in the fierce semi-finals of the Winter Continuous Track Cup, and they head to the finals, where they will face St. Gloriana Girls' College, led by Darjeeling. Among the members of St. Gloriana Girls' College is Alice, who transferred to St. Gloriana to be able to face Miho again.

Eiga Meitantei Precure! Fushigi na Niwa to Futari no Himitsu (Detective Precure! The Movie: The Mysterious Garden and the Secret of 2 People) — the film for Star Detective Precure! , the 23rd main anime entry in the Precure franchise — dropped from #5 to #9 in its fourth weekend.

The film opened in Japan on September 18. It sold 358,000 tickets to earn 446 million yen (about US$2.82 million) in its first three days. In its first six days until September 23, the film sold 606,000 tickets and earned 746 million yen (about US$4.71 million).

The cast members who voice the film's original characters are Akari Kitō as Karin, a 14-year-old girl who holds the key to the story; Nobunaga Shimazaki as Alan, a fairy who watches over Karin; and Kōki Uchiyama as Rain, a fairy who requests the Detective Precures' help.

Hanako Ueda ( You and Idol Precure♪ , Summer Time Rendering , My Hero Academia FINAL SEASON episode director) directed the film. Yoshimi Narita ( Eiga HappinessCharge PreCure! Ningyō no Kuni no Ballerina , Eiga Precure All Stars New Stage 3: Eien no Tomodachi , Eiga Tropical-Rouge! Precure: Yuki no Princess to Kiseki no Yubiwa! films) wrote the script, Erika Fukasawa ( Eiga Kimi to Idol Precure♪ Omatase! Kimi ni Todokeru Kirakkilive! ) and Misaki Umase ( You and Idol Precure♪ ) composed the music, and Emiko Miyamoto ( Eiga Precure All Stars F , Precure Super Stars! original character designer) designed the characters and was also the film's chief animation director.

Yūka Masui and Chihaya Yoshitake perform the film's ending theme song "FIRST PRISM." Ami Ishii performs the insert song "First Step."

Puella Magi Madoka Magica The Movie: Walpurgisnacht: Rising ( Gekijōban Mahō Shōjo Madoka Magica: Walpurgis no Kaiten ), the official sequel to the Puella Magi Madoka Magica The Movie Part 3: Rebellion film, dropped from #7 to #10 in its seventh weekend. The film earned 75,584,180 yen (about US$479,200) from Friday to Sunday, and has earned a cumulative total of 2,494,107,540 yen (about US$15.81 million).

The film got IMAX screenings in Japan on August 28, the same day it opened in theaters. The film sold 535,000 tickets and and earned 939,647,100 yen (about US$5.95 million) in its first three days.

Yukihiro Miyamoto ( Puella Magi Madoka Magica , Magia Record: Puella Magi Madoka Magica Side Story , Arakawa Under the Bridge ) directed the film.

Shion Wakayama voices the new magical girl Shichōka and Tomoyo Kurosawa voices Selma Therese.

The anime film features a returning staff from the original anime series and films, including original creators Magica Quartet , chief director Akiyuki Simbo , scriptwriter Gen Urobuchi of Nitroplus , original character designer Ume Aoki , animation character designer Junichirō Taniguchi , composer Yuki Kajiura , alternate space designer Gekidan Inu Curry , and animation studio SHAFT .

title: Demon Slayer Just Got Easier to Watch Than Ever With New Streaming Launch
content:
There’s still a while before fans get an update on the second installment of the Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle movie trilogy. However, before the anime returns, the official X handle confirms that all episodes are streaming on Prime Video. This includes the Mugen Train Arc, which was initially released as a movie and later broadcast as a TV series with extended scenes. The Hashira Training Arc is the final season of the anime since the series confirms adapting the Infinity Castle Arc into a movie trilogy. While the anime hasn’t shared any updates on the second part of the movie for over a year, the first installment of the Infinity Castle again made headlines in July and September after getting its streaming update.

All seasons and movies of the anime are already streaming on both Crunchyroll and Netflix. Crunchyroll is the official home for the series, while Netflix often delays the streaming dates outside of Asian regions. With Prime Video adding everything else except the latest movie, the anime became much easier to stream from home. We might also get an update on the platform licensing the latest movie before Part 2’s release.

Does Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle Part 2 Have a Release Date?

As of now, the anime hasn’t shared any updates on the second movie. Although the trilogy was announced in 2024, only the first film has been released so far. The first installment hit Japanese theatres in July 2025 before making a worldwide debut in September of the same year. While fans have been awaiting updates since then, the animation studio has stayed silent on the upcoming films. However, we can expect updates by the end of the year, especially during Jump Festa 2027, which will be held in December this year . It’s the largest convention for anime and manga fans held annually by Shueisha to reveal the latest updates on Shonen Jump series. The event this year will be held on December 19th and 20th, during which Demon Slayer will hold a panel on the Super Stage.

Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle Will Be More Intense Than Ever

The first movie only covered the initial phase of the Infinity Castle Arc. While the fights against Akaza and Kaigaku are over, Doma is still standing strong even after Shinobu used poison on him. The movie ends on a major cliffhanger as soon as Giyu and Tanjiro win against Akaza. The finale also sets up the upcoming battles in the arc while Nakime continues to shift the layout of the Infinity Castle to confuse the Demon Slayers. The Infinity Castle is the longest arc in the story, with several intense battles often leading to tragic conclusions. The final war against the demons was still in the initial phase during the first part, but everything will start to go downhill from here on out. The second movie will also focus on the fight against the Upper Moons since there’s still a while before Muzan enters the battlefield. The story is in its final stretch, and after the Infinity Castle Arc, the Sunrise Countdown will wrap up the battle.

title: Gundam Blitz Order Mobile Game Announced
content:
Bandai Namco Entertainment announced the new Gundam Blitz Order "RPG-style idle simulation" mobile game on Thursday.

English video

Japanese video

Bandai Namco Entertainment is currently accepting applications for a network test for the game that will take place from November 18-24.

The company has opened an English website and X/Twitter account for the game.

Bandai Namco Entertainment describes the game:

With Gundam Blitz Order , we're taking on a new challenge for Gundam games by developing the series' first idle game. While there are many different styles of idle games, Gundam Blitz Order is an RPG-style idle simulation game where players collect and strengthen mobile suit units, increase their combat power, and build strategic formations while considering the unique battle styles of each unit. While some players may be new to the idle game genre, it offers unique benefits that help reduce the burden of gameplay. For example, upgrade materials which are used to strengthen units can be collected automatically, allowing players to progress more easily. We hope many players will enjoy this new take on a Gundam game.

In the game, players develop their own Mobile Suits, warships, and Mobile Armors from across the Gundam franchise, and build a team of these units to lead them to victory.

title: Crunchyroll Adds English Dub for Saga of Tanya the Evil the Movie Anime
content:
Crunchyroll originally began streaming the film in September 2019.

Crunchyroll previously screened the film in more than 500 theaters in the United States in May 2019. It describes the story:

The time is UC 1926. The Imperial Army's 203rd Air Mage Battalion led by Major Tanya Degurechaff has won the battle to the south against the Republic's stragglers. They expected to be given a vacation after returning victorious, but instead receive special orders from Staff HQ as soon as they get home. They are told that there were signs of a large-scale deployment near the Empire-Federation border. Faced with the prospect of a new major enemy, the desperate Empire fans the flame of war. Meanwhile, an international volunteer army spearheaded by the Commonwealth set foot in Federation territory. As they say, the enemy of an enemy is your friend. They suffer through misfortune purely out of national interest, and among them is a young girl. She is Warrant Officer Mary Sue, and she takes up arms hoping to bring the Empire, who killed her father, to justice.

The film opened in Japan in February 2019.

Crunchyroll began streaming an English dub for The Saga of Tanya the Evil: Operation Desert Pasta special last month. The 17-minute short debuted during a livestreamed event for the franchise in June 2021. Crunchyroll added the short to its library in the same month.

The first television anime season premiered in January 2017. Crunchyroll streamed the series as it aired, and Funimation streamed an English dub.

Saga of Tanya the Evil II ( Yōjo Senki II ), the anime's second season , debuted on the AT-X channel on July 8. Crunchyroll is also streaming an English dub for the new season.
